A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAAC research work. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original learning experiments on six navigation benchmarks and synthetic informativeness results in Table 1 and Figure 2.

after.justification: Section 5 reports benchmark and redesigned synthetic experiments. Appendix E adds original policy-performance and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The IAAC framework remains, but v2 replaces direct HSCIC estimation with cross-fitted residual dependence testing and replaces the Bernstein-bound criterion with episode-level prediction-gain tests. Section 4.3 also specifies candidate-generator selection. These substantially revise the proposed signal-assessment procedures.

E1.justification: The six navigation tasks remain. Synthetic coverage changes from random rewards and noisy state embeddings to masked state features with explicitly controlled reward relevance. V2 also evaluates alternative observable feature subsets and observation-noise scenarios, substantially changing the represented synthetic signal and observation conditions.

E2.justification: The navigation comparisons retain A2C, asym-A2C-s and asym-A2C-hs. Both versions compare informed and history-only critics in synthetic studies. V2's additional privileged-signal configurations are ablations within the framework, rather than new baseline algorithms.

E3.justification: The redesigned synthetic tests use 20 rather than 10 states and 250 rather than 20 random-policy episodes. Prediction evaluation changes from 25,000 training episodes of length 50 to 2,500 episodes of length 25 with five-fold validation; synthetic critics change from Elman RNNs with a 256-unit hidden layer to GRUs with linear readouts. Appendix E.1 adds a 15,000-step control-training protocol. Navigation distance signals are described as Manhattan rather than Earth Mover's distance, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: V1's privileged-noise and confidence-level/instance analyses are replaced by feature-relevance comparisons and Appendix E's policy-performance linkage, observation-noise robustness tests and alternative-observation-feature analysis. These investigate substantial new questions about signal selection and its practical consequences.

E5.justification: V2 replaces raw-signal permutations with episode-level residual permutations, increases the stated permutation count from 30 to 1,000, and adds the finite-permutation p-value correction. Episode-level bootstrap or one-sided t-tests replace the Bernstein confidence bound. Synthetic summaries shift from variation across POMDP instances to ten-run statistics on a sampled environment; benchmark reporting retains 20-run means and standard deviations.

E6.justification: Figure 1's benchmark curves are retained, but v1's HSCIC results and Bernstein-bound distributions are replaced by feature-specific scores and new policy/robustness results. For example, v2 Table 1 reports prediction gains of 0.064 ± 0.020 for [s1,s2,s4,s5] and 0.056 ± 0.032 for full state. Tables 3–5 and Figures 2–3 add further findings. These are results under redesigned settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The IAAC unbiasedness theorem and full-state corollaries remain. V2 replaces the HSCIC/Bernstein definitions and adds surrogate-null propositions and regression-error bounds in Appendix B. Remark 2.1 adds an observation-plus-auxiliary construction, while v1's state-augmentation argument is removed. The new justification has a material mismatch: Section 4.1 uses unconditional residual independence, whereas Proposition B.1 establishes conditional independence.

C1.justification: The central claims—unbiased asymmetric learning with partial privileged information and competitive performance against full-state critics—remain. The advertised informativeness contribution is refined from direct HSCIC testing to residual testing, with more explicit emphasis on selecting signal generators.

C2.justification: V1 mainly emphasizes instance-dependent usefulness. V2 adds substantive discussion of surrogate-null limitations, regression-error sensitivity, history-encoder requirements, and why reduced state uncertainty need not make value approximation easier. Appendix E interprets informativeness as an imperfect proxy for control improvement and explains effects of observation noise and feature choice.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project source-code link, residual-test pseudocode, synthetic feature-generation equations, and concrete settings including 100-tree random forests, five-fold fitting, 512 Nyström landmarks and synthetic learning rates. V1's PyRKHSstats implementation disclosure is removed with its HSCIC procedure. Navigation architecture, hardware and Table 2 hyperparameters are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the research context with latent-representation methods, racing and plasma-control applications, and additional privileged-RL convergence theory. It adds residual-testing and Nyström-HSIC references while removing earlier kernel-embedding/HSCIC references. Positioning IAAC as a generalization of history-state critics remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and background receive extensive rewriting. Related Work is integrated into the Introduction, actor-critic explanations expand, and experiments are reorganized into benchmark-performance and informativeness-validation sections. The appendices are substantially reorganized around the revised theory and analyses.

P2.justification: V1's Figure 2 boxplots are removed; v2 adds a three-panel training figure and informativeness-versus-performance scatterplots. Table 1 is redesigned to juxtapose both criteria, and Tables 3–5 plus Algorithm 1 are added. Figure 1 is retained and resized, alongside substantial changes to text width, spacing and placement.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful implementation information, episode-level statistical procedures and direct analyses connecting signal scores to policy learning. However, it replaces multi-instance synthetic validation with studies centered on a sampled environment. Its revised residual test also relies on an unresolved mismatch between unconditional independence in Section 4.1 and conditional independence in Proposition B.1. Because this affects a central revised contribution, the empirical and documentation gains do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
